headline: Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway blocked by workers' protest over unpaid wages
summary: Workers of Talha Spinning Mill staged a blockade near MC Bazar in Sreepur, Gazipur, leaving passengers and transport operators stranded.
details: Workers of Talha Spinning Mill staged a protest late Thursday night by blocking the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur.
The blockade, which began around 11:00 PM near MC Bazar, caused severe traffic congestion on both sides of the highway, leaving passengers and transport operators stranded.
Protesting workers claim their salaries for May have not yet been cleared despite repeated assurances from the factory authorities.
Mohammad Kamruzzaman, officer-in-charge of Maona Highway Police Station, confirmed that the workers were continuing the blockade as of midnight.
Police are currently discussing the matter with both the workers and the factory management in an effort to resolve the issue and restore traffic flow.
caption:
A highway blockade by factory workers over unpaid May salaries has brought traffic to a standstill in Gazipur.

Workers of Talha Spinning Mill staged a protest late Thursday night by blocking the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur.

The blockade, which began around 11:00 PM near MC Bazar, caused severe traffic congestion on both sides of the highway, leaving passengers and transport operators stranded.

Protesting workers claim their salaries for May have not yet been cleared despite repeated assurances from the factory authorities.

Mohammad Kamruzzaman, officer-in-charge of Maona Highway Police Station, confirmed that the workers were continuing the blockade as of midnight.

Police are currently discussing the matter with both the workers and the factory management in an effort to resolve the issue and restore traffic flow.

headline_marked: Beximco Pharma [[faces delisting risk from London Stock Exchange]] after 5-month suspension
headline: Beximco Pharma faces delisting risk from London Stock Exchange after 5-month suspension
summary: Trading of the company's GDRs has been suspended since January for failing to publish audited financial statements, with a critical two-week window remaining to avoid removal.
details: Trading of Beximco Pharmaceuticals on the London Stock Exchange's (LSE) Alternative Investment Market (AIM) has been suspended for five and a half months. The company is now just two weeks away from potential delisting.

The suspension began on January 2 after the company failed to publish its annual report within the regulatory deadline. The delay was attributed to board meeting delays caused by a legal dispute over a BSEC proposal to appoint independent directors.
Under AIM Rule 41, securities suspended for six consecutive months may face cancellation of admission to trading. The six-month threshold ends on July 2, creating a high-risk window for the company.
BSEC Chairman Masud Khan warned that delisting would damage Bangladesh's capital market reputation and create difficulties for other Bangladeshi companies seeking overseas listings.
Six institutional investors of Beximco Pharma's Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) have urged the BSEC for a 'dignified resolution' to the issue.
The BSEC is now working to arrange an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) with court approval to publish the audited financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2025, within the next two weeks.
Despite the suspension in London, trading of Beximco Pharma shares continues normally on the Dhaka Stock Exchange and Chittagong Stock Exchange.
caption:
Beximco Pharma is just two weeks away from being delisted from the London Stock Exchange. A failure to publish financial reports has triggered a crisis.

Trading of Beximco Pharmaceuticals on the London Stock Exchange's (LSE) Alternative Investment Market (AIM) has been suspended for five and a half months. The company is now just two weeks away from potential delisting.

The suspension began on January 2 after the company failed to publish its annual report within the regulatory deadline. The delay was attributed to board meeting delays caused by a legal dispute over a BSEC proposal to appoint independent directors.

Under AIM Rule 41, securities suspended for six consecutive months may face cancellation of admission to trading. The six-month threshold ends on July 2, creating a high-risk window for the company.

BSEC Chairman Masud Khan warned that delisting would damage Bangladesh's capital market reputation and create difficulties for other Bangladeshi companies seeking overseas listings.

Six institutional investors of Beximco Pharma's Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) have urged the BSEC for a 'dignified resolution' to the issue.

The BSEC is now working to arrange an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) with court approval to publish the audited financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2025, within the next two weeks.

Despite the suspension in London, trading of Beximco Pharma shares continues normally on the Dhaka Stock Exchange and Chittagong Stock Exchange.
